title: US infant mortality rate, 2025 provisional
question: CDC/NCHS Vital Statistics Rapid Release quarterly provisional infant mortality rate, Rates by Age, Infant mortality, 12-month-ending 2025 Q4, first print
resolutionSource: CDC/NCHS Vital Statistics Rapid Release, Quarterly Provisional Estimates for Infant Mortality
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first CDC/NCHS published value in dataset jqwm-z2g9 for topic 'Rates by Age', indicator 'Infant mortality', time_period '12 Month-ending', year_and_quarter '2025 Q4', in deaths under age 1 per 1,000 live births, rounded to the agency's two-decimal published precision. Use the first official print and do not substitute later revisions.
drivers: pre-release 12-month-ending series was trending lower through 2025 Q3
persistence from the latest available 2025 Q3 value dominates the forecast
recent one-quarter declines averaged about 0.03 points
interval widened modestly for provisional reporting and first-print uncertainty

reasoning.text: US 2025 provisional infant mortality first print

Framing and exact resolver: this targets the CDC/NCHS VSRR infant mortality dashboard, not final linked birth/infant death file data. The variant is Rates by Age, Infant mortality, 12 Month-ending, 2025 Q4, with rates per 1,000 live births and two-decimal agency rounding.

reasoning.call: Opened CDC/NCHS infant mortality dashboard notes and source metadata available for the public VSRR series.
reasoning.result: Dashboard states infant mortality rates are deaths under age 1 per 1,000 live births; estimates for 2025 are provisional; the relevant dashboard covers 2023 through Quarter 4 2025 and uses rates per 1,000 live births.

reasoning.call: Opened CDC/NCHS 2026 statistical release calendar for the scheduled first release date.
reasoning.result: Calendar lists 05/26/26 for 'Quarterly Provisional Estimates of Infant Mortality: 2023 - Q4 2025' and 07/29/26 for the next Q1 2026 update.

reasoning.call: Fetched CDC Socrata dataset jqwm-z2g9 for pre-resolution Rates by Age, Infant mortality, 12 Month-ending values through 2025 Q3 only.
Fetched recent comparable annual-window observations from the same CDC/NCHS VSRR series for the local trend reference class.
reasoning.result: Fetched latest comparable values before the target: 2024 Q4 5.54, 2025 Q1 5.50, 2025 Q2 5.46, 2025 Q3 5.45.

reasoning.text: Reference class/base rate: the directly comparable official annual-window infant mortality observations before the 2025 Q4 target show a gradual decline from 5.69 in 2023 Q1 to 5.45 in 2025 Q3, with the last four pre-target annual-window values at 5.54, 5.50, 5.46, and 5.45.

Prior/update/interval: persistence prior was the latest available 2025 Q3 annual-window rate of 5.45. Historical sample was 2023 Q1 through 2025 Q3 from the same Rates by Age, Infant mortality, 12 Month-ending variant. Successive changes were 0.00, -0.04, -0.02, -0.02, 0.00, -0.05, -0.02, -0.04, -0.04, -0.01, so sigma = 0.018; 1.28*sigma = 0.023. I apply a -0.03 momentum adjustment, close to the recent average quarterly annual-window decline, giving 5.42. I widen to a 0.04 half-width, about 1.7x the raw half-width, for first-print provisional uncertainty and uneven quarterly reporting, implying 5.38 to 5.46.
Level and momentum: the 12-month-ending level had eased from 5.54 in 2024 Q4 to 5.45 in 2025 Q3, so a further but not abrupt decline is the central pre-release expectation.

Counter-considerations: upside risk would come from late reporting or a rebound in neonatal deaths that leaves the first print above 5.46; downside risk would come from a broader decline in postneonatal or SIDS deaths and would land below the interval if the first print were under 5.38.

Review disposition: accepted the leakage, update, interval, prior/update/interval, and historical-context critiques by excluding the 2025 Q4 target value and components, keeping the CDC/NCHS resolver unchanged, and recomputing the point and interval from pre-release history through 2025 Q3 only.
